messages:
lina-support: FYI ACME-prod reports a sudden latency + billing spike, all EU traffic started landing in us-east around 09:32 UTC. customer sees 200-600ms extra p99 + some 401s. request ids: r-9a2b,r-9a2c. Can SRE triage?
acme-app: Confirmed. Started ~09:30. Region header in our requests is eu-west-1, but we see backend logs showing us-east hostnames. Latency for chat endpoints jumped from ~60ms to ~420ms.
sam-sre: Looking. Any recent config changes or migrations to routing/policy?
lina-support: We pushed the failover-policy migration last night (migration v2 -> v3) via console-migrate. Nora might know details.
nora-product: Yep, we ran the policy schema migration at 02:40 UTC. It changed priority encoding and started stringifying weights for compatibility with the UI. We tested locally but not at scale.
sam-sre: I pulled the effective policy for ACME-prod key via rtsctl:
```
policy: {
  "priority": ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"],
  "weights": {"us-east-1": "90", "eu-west-1": "10"},
  "sticky": true
}
```
That looks wrong — priority order is inverted for an EU key. Expected eu-west first.
acme-app: That's the crux — they always had eu-west pref. We never changed client-side.
sam-sre: Checking migration script... aha: migration serialized priority arrays using Object.keys on a map built from regions, which produced insertion-order based on how the map was constructed. During console import the UI populated regions in a different order, flipping the array. Also weights are strings; our router assumes numeric parse and does lexicographic sort when weights are strings in a couple of older code paths. That caused an accidental promotion of us-east.
nora-product: Ugh. So two issues: array reorder during migration + stringified weights causing unexpected tie/weight handling.
lina-support: Customer wants rollback or hotfix asap. They flagged billing team.
mike-billing: ACME opened a billing dispute; we need to provide timeline and mitigations. If we can confirm region misrouting we can offer credits. Keep me posted.
sam-sre: Mitigation steps I'm pushing now: 1) apply an override policy pinned for acme-prod that explicitly sets priority order eu-west-1 first, weight numbers as integers; 2) flush route-cache for that key; 3) short TTL (5m) until migration bug fixed. Commands I'm running:
```
rtsctl set-override --key acme-prod --policy '{"priority":["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],"weights":{"eu-west-1":90,"us-east-1":10},"sticky":true}'
rtsctl flush-cache --key acme-prod
rtsctl set-ttl --key acme-prod --route-override-ttl 300
```
acme-app: Thanks, please confirm once routing flips — we can monitor.
deploy-bot: deploy #rts-rollback-299 started by sam-sre — rolling override to 3 hosts.
sam-sre: Override applied. Flushed cache. Waiting for propagation (expected <1m).
acme-app: Seeing eu-west hits again. p99 back to ~70ms. 401s gone. Thanks.
lina-support: Customer happy for now but wants root cause and a permanent fix.
nora-product: I'll open a migration rollback + fix PR. Proposed permanent fix: ensure migration preserves array order from source canonical list and convert string weights to ints at write-time. Also add a fast validation that priorities align with key region preferences during migration.
sam-sre: Agreed. I'll run audit to find other keys affected and a script to auto-apply overrides for any mismatch.
mike-billing: I'll freeze billing escalation for ACME and draft a credit proposal; need final affected window timestamps.
lina-support: Window: 2026-03-12T09:30:00Z -> 2026-03-12T09:39:10Z per logs (patched at ~09:34 + propagation).
nora-product: Filing INCIDENT-2026-0312-RMIG with RCA tasks and patch ETA EOD. Will add tests covering string-weight parse and priority ordering.
sam-sre: I'll follow up with a list of affected API keys once audit completes.
lina-support: Thanks team. acme-app: appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
